the nuclear pairing correlations in rotating nuclei are strongly influenced by the single-particle structure and, in particular, by the presence of the single-particle states with the large orbital angular momentum L.

(a) The state-dependent pairing interaction, when combined with a realistic single-particle Hamiltonian, leads to a rich structure of low-lying states with a variety of quantum numbers and properties.

the development of a theoretical framework that allows to study the dynamics of quantum systems in the presence of strong correlations.

the method presented here is an efficient, accurate, and reliable tool for the study of the nuclear mean-field and state-dependent pairing Hamiltonians.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have constructed and implemented an algorithm for the diagonalization of the pairing problem in a many-body space with a precision of (1-2)% and with the computational time on the order of seconds.
we developed a method to solve the nuclear pairing problem in a deformed Woods-Saxton potential with the state-dependent monpole pairing force.
we have developed a new method for solving the nuclear mean-field + pairing problem.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the state-dependent pairing interaction can be treated in a particle-number conserving way.
the state-dependent pairing interaction can be treated with the same accuracy as the standard BCS pairing Hamiltonian.

a particle-number-conserving approach can provide an accurate solution of the nuclear mean-field problem with a realistic single-particle potential in the many-body space corresponding to 40 particles on 80 levels, with a precision of about 2%.
